title: Adaptive governor policy assembler for throughput targets and safety floodgates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity need predictable throughput guarantees while the autoscaler must avoid oscillation and costly overprovisioning. Current autoscale policies are pointwise (single-metric) and do not compose headroom credits, latency SLAs, and burst fences into a single executable policy. This ticket scopes a new 'policy assembler' that compiles high-level SLOs (throughput target, p99 latency, cost ceiling) into a runtime-governor config: target metrics, blending algorithm (composite targets), and safety floodgates (max-step, cooldown windows, debt ledger). The assembler should produce an opinionated JSON policy that the autoscaler can interpret and enforce across dedicated fleets.
decisions: Use a composite target model: weighted combination of throughput-percentile and latency-band occupancy rather than single-metric setpoints
Implement a two-stage scaling algorithm: conservative ramp (PID-like) for steady-state, and fast-exit surge for burst completion with strict budget accounting

Safety floodgates will include: max-scale-step (absolute GPUs), rate-limit per minute, cooldown window, headroom-credit ledger, and emergency shed circuit. Default values are conservative and tunable per-tenant
tradeoffs: Aggressive surge behavior reduces latency but increases short-term cost; we prioritize latency for P0 customers and cost for P2 tiers
A more complex composite metric improves stability but raises configuration surface area; the policy assembler will provide presets (balanced/latency-first/cost-first)

Keeping decision logic in the control plane (assembler) simplifies fleet runtime but increases control-plane computation; initial version will assemble offline at rollout time and push compiled policies to runtime

2026-03-02 Kai Morgan: Implemented synthesis prototype that generates composite targets from percentile histograms. Early tests on staging fleet show reduced oscillation.
2026-03-04 Design review (Luca Hernandez): Suggested clearer visualization for headroom ledger in Console; flagged UX ticket.
2026-03-08 SRE feedback (Maya Singh): Request adding a hard global upper-bound step to avoid noisy autoscale storms during regional networking events.

2026-03-10 Engineering review: Agreed to default cooldown of 90s, max-step of 4 GPUs for small fleets, and headroom decay half-life of 15 minutes. Added dependency on predictive warmup infra (ENG-612345).
acceptance_criteria: Assembler produces valid compiled policy JSON for three presets: balanced, latency-first, cost-first
Autoscaler runtime accepts compiled policy and performs scaling decisions consistent with policy fields (unit tests + integration tests)
Staging benchmark: p99 latency does not regress more than 5% and scaling step variance reduces by 30% vs baseline over 6-hour synthetic workload
Console surfaces policy fields and headroom ledger metrics; UX placeholder is acceptable for MVP
